hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.text:
Great! To help you determine your Child Benefit eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

**First, let me ask about the child you're applying for:**

**How old is the child?** This will help me determine which eligibility path applies:
- Under 16 years old?
- Between 16-19 years old?
- 20 years old or over?

Please tell me the age of the child (or children if you have multiple) you're inquiring about.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 18 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex who is 18 years old and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 18 (which falls in the 16-19 age range), his eligibility will depend on whether he meets certain education or training requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to understand Alex's current situation regarding education or training:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (attending a course or program)?
2. **Recently left education** (within the last few months)?
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and didn't recently leave?

Which of these applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in education or training anymore - he finished school and he's not doing any courses now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex has left education, I need to check if he left recently enough to potentially qualify for an extension period.

**When did Alex leave education or training?** 

Specifically, has it been:
- Within the last 20 weeks (about 5 months)?
- Or longer than 20 weeks ago?

This matters because there's a potential extension period for young people who have recently left education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was quite recent - just a couple of months ago actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Good to know - a couple of months ago would be within the 20-week timeframe. Let me check the extension eligibility criteria for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see the extension rules now. There's an important detail here:

**The 20-week extension period is specifically for children aged 16-17 who have left education.** 

However, since Alex is already 18 years old, this extension doesn't apply to him. The extension ends when the child turns 18, whichever comes first.

Let me also ask - **is Alex currently in any approved education or training program?** This is important because if he's enrolled in an approved course, different rules would apply. If he's not in any education or training and is 18, I need to make sure I have all the information correct.

To confirm:
- Alex is 18 years old
- He left education a couple of months ago
- He is NOT currently in any education or training program

Is that all correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's all correct. He's 18, left school a couple of months ago, and he's not doing any education or training now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that information. Based on what you've told me, let me navigate through the eligibility criteria.

conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment Result

I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** based on his current circumstances.

### Why Alex Doesn't Qualify:

**For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit is only available if they are enrolled in approved education or training.** Since Alex:
- Is 18 years old
- Left education a couple of months ago
- Is not currently in any approved education or training program

He does not meet the qualifying child criteria.

### About the Extension Period:

There is a 20-week extension period available for young people aged 16-17 who leave education and register with qualifying services (like government careers services, Connexions, or armed services). However, **this extension ends when the child turns 18**, whichever comes sooner. Since Alex is already 18, this extension doesn't apply to him.

### What This Means:

If you were previously receiving Child Benefit for Alex, it would have stopped when he either:
- Turned 18, or
- Left approved education (if he was already 18)

### Possible Next Steps:

If Alex decides to return to approved education or training in the future, you may be able to reclaim Child Benefit. Approved education includes courses such as:
- A-levels or similar qualifications
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to level 3
- Home education (if it started before the child turned 16)

The course must be full-time (more than 12 hours per week of supervised study).

If you have any questions or if Alex's circumstances change, you can find more information at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility
